title: Chip Price-Hike Domino: Wafers, onsemi, Renesas and Record DDR5 - Where Samsung and SK hynix Fit
content:
Korea Supply Chain Brief · September 27, 2026

Price increases are moving through the chip supply chain, from silicon wafers and gases to power chips, while DDR5 spot prices sit at a record. A Money Today report laid out the chain. Here is who is raising prices at each layer, what the source is for each claim, and where Korea's Samsung Electronics and SK hynix fit.

The chain, layer by layer

LayerWhat is happeningSource
Silicon wafersPrices for all wafer sizes expected to rise at least 10%, the first increase in three yearsTaiwanese media, as cited by Money Today (outlook, not confirmed)
Gases, chemicals, packaging materialsPrices rising, including protective packaging for chipsIndustry, per Money Today
Power semiconductorsonsemi (NASDAQ: ON) told customers it will raise prices across a broad range of products from October 10Industry sources, per Money Today
Automotive chipsRenesas (TSE: 6723) has announced price increases for next yearCompany statement, per Money Today
Passive components and industrial gasPrice moves spreading to MLCCs (multilayer ceramic capacitors) and industrial gasesMoney Today (no companies named)
DRAMDDR5 16Gb spot price hit US$56.9 on September 21, a record; up 5.6% this month and roughly double since JanuaryMoney Today

Why prices are rising

onsemi cited higher raw material, manufacturing, energy and infrastructure costs, combined with stronger demand for power, industrial and data center chips. Renesas described structural cost pressure across raw materials, energy, advanced packaging, capacity and logistics. The common driver is AI data center investment, which is pulling demand through parts of the supply chain that used to get little attention, and giving those suppliers more leverage in price talks.

Where Korea fits

The report's Korean angle is memory. Its analysis is that the price wave may help Samsung Electronics (KRX: 005930) and SK hynix (KRX: 000660) more than it hurts them:

  • Higher wafer and packaging costs are a burden, but current memory margins are high enough to absorb them.
  • Widespread price increases are themselves a sign that chip supply is tight.
  • Some analysts argue the recent DRAM price surge has not yet been fully reflected in HBM prices, leaving room for further HBM increases.
  • JP Morgan projects HBM supply will fall 19% short of demand next year.

These points are the reporter's analysis and a bank forecast, not company guidance. The report does not name any Korean wafer, gas, MLCC or packaging supplier as raising prices, so we do not name one either.

Quick FAQ

Is onsemi raising prices?
According to industry sources cited by Money Today, onsemi notified customers of price increases across a broad range of products effective October 10, 2026.

What is the DDR5 spot price now?
DDR5 16Gb spot traded at US$56.9 on September 21, 2026, a record, according to the report.

Does this help Samsung and SK hynix?
The report argues it may, because memory margins can absorb higher input costs and the price hikes signal tight supply. That is analysis, not a forecast from the companies.
